statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Nasdaq-100 conditions remain narrow and orderly roughly five hours before the US August employment report at 12:30 UTC.
recommendation: The assessment favours a narrow evidence-based danger window around the payrolls release rather than a session-wide restriction; Tail remains below the block threshold on current evidence.
headline: Narrow, orderly pre-payrolls range with a modestly softer European open and no observed one-way structure
body: NQ futures trade near 29,613, about +0.30%, inside an overnight range of roughly 29,482 to 29,644 that spans only about 0.55%. The most recent hourly band is narrower still, near 29,575 to 29,644, and the drift holds the upper half of the range without repeated extension, so retracement opportunity is intact. Europe opened modestly softer, with the Stoxx 600 down 0.18% and Nasdaq-100 futures up about 0.17% on the day, which is a two-sided rather than aligned configuration. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Sep 3 at 29,482.32, up 1.16%, in a day range of 29,160.96 to 29,538.76, after Fed Governor Christopher Waller signalled he could support a September hold if inflation data does not surprise. That cut the share of fed funds futures pricing a September hike to about 50.4% from roughly 63.2% a day earlier and pulled Treasury yields lower. The H.15 release for Sep 2 shows the 2-year at 4.39% and the 10-year at 4.79%, both easing on Sep 3. VIX closed at 14.32, showing no volatility bid. Internals on Sep 3 were broad but dispersed: megacaps were higher across the board except Broadcom, which fell about 4% after pairing an earnings beat with soft fiscal fourth-quarter revenue guidance, while Snowflake rose more than 20%. That pattern argues for rotation rather than single-direction index pressure. Two standing macro threads are carried as Stress rather than as evidence of a pathological path. WTI near $91.6 with Brent near $95.8 is up roughly 9% to 10% on the week on renewed US-Iran hostilities and restricted Strait of Hormuz transits, without so far transmitting into sustained index downside. And the August Employment Situation at 12:30 UTC is the defining checkpoint, with consensus near +53K payrolls against a prior two-month net loss of 3K and an unemployment rate consensus of 4.1%, on an unusually wide estimate range from a 25K loss to a 121K gain. Consistent with the framework, event importance and forecast dispersion are scored into Stress and Confidence rather than into assessed pathological price-path risk until persistent one-way structure is actually observed. Shared latest-session cross-asset context was consulted but was about two hours old at assessment time, beyond the freshness threshold for supporting use, so it was weighted only as background and the picture above rests on independently verified current sources.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours are fully covered by published Claude assessments. Conditions were benign through the European session on Sep 3 with Tail near 13 and the mode assessed as normal. The mode shifted to trend-up across the US cash session with Tail peaking at 21 as the Waller-driven rally developed, then decayed through the US evening as the move matured. Overnight into Sep 4 the mode returned to normal, Tail held between 12 and 15 and Stress eased into the low 50s before edging back up as the payrolls report drew closer.
outlookSummary: The baseline path holds a low-amplitude range through the European session, with Stress building mechanically into the 12:30 UTC August employment report. The release hour and the following digestion hour, which contains the 13:30 UTC cash open, carry the widest two-sided repricing risk of the window and are modelled at Tail 23 and 24, which map to WATCH rather than to a block. That is consistent with the framework treating event importance and forecast dispersion as Stress and Confidence inputs until persistent one-way structure is actually observed, and with a two-sided rate distribution that favours whipsaw over sustained direction. Tail is modelled decaying through the US afternoon as the release is absorbed, with a small uplift into the final cash hour on squaring ahead of the Labor Day holiday on Sep 7. CME equity index futures halt for the weekend at 21:00 UTC, so the last nine slots carry a closed-market floor with Confidence stepped down to reflect the absence of a live price path. The principal invalidation of this outlook would be observed post-release continuation with shallow or failed retracements, particularly through the 13:30 UTC cash open.

Two-sided pricing argues for whipsaw rather than one sustained direction on a surprise.
